hypotheses.reasoning: At 22:04:17 session-cache was replaced and came back empty because there was no RDB snapshot. Right after that, account-svc's cache miss ratio jumped from about 6% to 93–99%, so it loaded every request from accounts-db. accounts-db then hit 490/500 connections and 98–100% CPU, and simple lookups slowed to several seconds. account-svc queries started timing out at 5000ms, and edge-proxy returned 504s on /login (#3049 onward). This is a cache stampede. Separate noise that doesn't explain this: the template-svc/mailer circuit breaker, the legacy-inventory healthcheck, and metrics-agent dropping samples.
accounts-db ran out of connection slots and CPU. But it only overloaded once the cache went cold.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm session-cache again, or limit how fast account-svc can load from the database, using request coalescing or a concurrency limit. Shed /login load until accounts-db recovers. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence, or pre-warm the cache before a replaced node takes traffic.
